Author: Dees (R)

Title: Frank Broyles Publicity Rights Protection Act
Author: Richardson S (R)
Topics: Deepfake, Effect on Labor/Employment, Private Sector Use

Title: Arkansas Kids Online Safety Act
Author: Collins A (D)
Summary: Provides that a covered platform shall take reasonable measures in the design and operation of any product, service, or feature that the platform knows is used by minors to avoid any heightened risk of harm to minors, including anxiety, depression, and suicidal behaviors, provides that parental tools provided by a covered platform shall include the ability to manage a minors privacy and account settings, creates the Kids Online Safety Council, provides for filter bubble transparency requirements.

Title: Criminal Offenses

Title: Arkansas Kids Online Safety Act
Author: Gramlich (R)
Summary: Creates the Arkansas Kids Online Safety Act, provides that a covered platform shall take reasonable measures in the design and operation of any product, service, or feature that the covered platform knows is used by minors to avoid any heightened risk of harm to minors caused by such product, service, or feature, including without limitation the mental health disorders, consistent with evidence-informed medical information.

Title: Model Training and Content Generated by Generative AI
Author: Richardson S (R)
Summary: Relates to the ownership of model training and content generated by a generative artificial intelligence tool, provides that, with certain exceptions, when a person uses a generative artificial intelligence tool to generate content, the person who provides the input or directive to the generative artificial intelligence tool shall be the owner of the generated content, provided that the content does not infringe on existing copyrights or intellectual property rights.

Title: Companion Chatbots
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Require a companion chatbot operator to take the above actions when it has constructive knowledge that a user is a minor. Requires an operator to prevent its companion chatbot from producing or facilitating the exchange of any sexually explicit material or proposing sexually explicit conduct.

Title: Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Relates to copyrighted materials. Requires a developer of a generative artificial intelligence model to document any covered materials that the developer knows were used by the developer to train the model. Requires the developer to make available a mechanism on the developer's website allowing a rights owner to submit a request for information. Authorizes a rights owner who complies with specified requirements for submitting a request that is not provided with information to bring a civil action.

Title: Local Agencies: Automated Decision Systems
Author: Cabaldon (D)
Summary: Imposes certain restrictions on the use of an automated decision system by a local agency to confer supportive services, permits, or licenses. Includes a prohibition on using an output from the system as the sole basis for an adverse eligibility or benefit determination affecting a natural person, except as specified. Requires the local agency to verify the accuracy of the system's outputs and to promote nondiscrimination in its use.

Title: Generative Artificial Intelligence
Author: Umberg (D)
Summary: Obligates an attorney who uses generative artificial intelligence to practice law to ensure that confidential personal identifying, or other nonpublic information, is not entered into a public generative artificial intelligence system. Requires an attorney to ensure that reasonable steps are taken to verify the accuracy of generative artificial intelligence material and to correct any erroneous or hallucinated output in any material used by the attorney.

Title: California Institutes for Science and Innovation
Author: Wiener (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law authorizes the Regents of the University of California to establish 4 California Institutes for Science and Innovation at separate campuses of the University of California for specified purposes. Provides that existing law authorizes the concentration of each institute to include, among other concentrations, medicine, bioengineering, or space. Authorizes the concentration of an institute to include artificial intelligence.

Title: Department of Technology: Inventory
Author: Cabaldon (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law, until January 1, 2029, requires the Department of Technology to annually submit to certain legislative committees a report regarding a specified required comprehensive inventory of all high-risk automated decision systems that have been, or are being, used, developed, or procured by a state agency. Extends that reporting requirement until January 1, 2032.

Title: California AI Standards and Safety Commission
Author: McNerney (D)
Topics: Government Use, Oversight/Governance, Private Sector Use
Summary: Require the agency to establish the California AI Standards and Safety Commission and would provide for its membership. Requires the commission to take certain actions related to the safety of artificial intelligence, including maintaining formal liaison relationships with state agencies deploying or procuring artificial intelligence, providing artificial intelligence technical expertise and artificial intelligence risk assessment.

Title: Toys: Companion Chatbots
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Prohibits, until 1/1/2031, the manufacture, sale, exchange, possession with intent to sell or exchange, and exposition or offer for sale or exchange to a retailer a toy, as defined, that includes a companion chatbot, and would make violations of the bill subject to the same civil liability as violations of the provisions applicable to operators of companion chatbots in the above-described paragraph.

Title: California Environmental Quality Act: Environmental
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Authorizes the Governor to certify a geothermal powerplant that meets certain criteria as an environmental leadership development project. Requires the quantification and mitigation of impacts for emissions of greenhouse gases of a data center project in the same manner as certain environmental leadership projects.

Title: Mental Health Professionals: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Regulates the use of artificial intelligence by licensed professionals providing psychotherapy services. Prohibits an individual, corporation, or entity from using artificial intelligence to record or transcribe psychotherapeutic communications or sessions or to triage or screen a person for the need for psychotherapy services unless the patient or their authorized representative is informed that artificial intelligence will be used and provides consent.

Title: Civil Actions: Housing Development Projects
Author: Ashby (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law provides that in a civil action brought by a plaintiff to challenge a housing development project that meets or exceeds the requirements for low or moderate income housing, a defendant may seek an order requiring the plaintiff to furnish an undertaking as security for costs and damages. Provides that existing law authorizes the court to limit the amount of the undertaking or to decline that requirement under certain conditions. Applies provisions to a student housing development.

Title: California State University: Faculty Employees
Author: Cervantes (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law requires certain community college employees to be a person who meets specified minimum qualifications. Requires the instructor of record for a course of instruction to be a person who meets the rule provided by the Trustees of the California State University to serve as a faculty employee teaching credit instruction or noncredit instruction.

Title: Employment: Automated Decision Systems
Author: McNerney (D)
Summary: Requires an employer that primarily relied upon an ADS to make a disciplinary, termination, or deactivation decision to provide the affected worker with a written postuse notice, as specified.

Title: Employment: Technological Displacement: Notice
Author: Reyes (D)
Topics: Effect on Labor/Employment, Notification, Private Sector Use
Summary: Requires an employer to provide a written technology hiring disruption notice to the Employment Development Department and the local workforce investment board when it executes a technological cessation in hiring directly and primarily due to the adoption of artificial intelligence or other automating technology. Imposes various reporting requirements on the Employment Development Department.

Title: California AI Transparency Act
Author: Becker (D)
Summary: Provides that the California AI Transparency Act requires a covered provider to make available an AI detection tool at no cost to the user. Provides that existing law requires a covered provider to include a certain latent disclosure in AI generated image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination thereof, created by the covered providers GenAI system. Requires a covered provider to include in the latent disclosure whether the content is generated or modified by artificial intelligence.

Title: Energy: Utility Infrastructure AI Safety
Author: McNerney (D)
Summary: Requires every public utility to furnish and maintain adequate, efficient, just, and reasonable service, instrumentalities, equipment, and facilities, as are necessary to promote the safety, health, comfort, and convenience of its customers, its employees, and the public. Requires the commission, on or before a specified date, to adopt standards for an electrical or gas corporation's use of artificial intelligence models, as provided.

Title: Crimes: Minors
Author: Strickland (R)
Summary: Makes any adult person who recruits, induces, coerces, or persuades a minor to commit an illegal act against another minor, or to solicit physical harm, sexual conduct, or images of an intimate body part, from another minor, or who utilizes a minor as a conduit of communication to facilitate any such acts guilty of a crime punishable either as a misdemeanor or a felony. Relates to images of an intimate body part that is produced by artificial intelligence and depicts the identity of another minor.

Title: False Advertising: Synthetic Digital Performers
Author: Ashby (D)
Summary: Makes it an unlawful advertising practice for a person to create and cause to be published in an advertising medium an advertisement that includes a synthetic performer without a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the performer is synthetic. Prohibits an advertising medium from transmitting, distributing, displaying, airing, or otherwise making available an advertisement containing a synthetic performer if a court of competent jurisdiction has issued an order.

Title: Covered Provider: Goods and Services: Self Preferencing
Status: Pending - Senate Privacy, Digital Technologies, and Consumer Protection Committee
Author: Wiener (D)
Summary: Prohibits a covered provider from preferencing its own products, services, or lines of business over those of another business user, including manipulating the order of search results or rankings to favor the products or services of the covered provider. Prohibits a covered provider from restricting interoperability or data portability, including restricting a business user or consumer from obtaining a copy of their data in a useful and portable format. Relates to actions for civil or criminal penalties.

Title: Digital Replicas
Author: Ashby (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law creates a civil cause of action against any person who knowingly uses the name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness of another person, without their consent, for specified purposes. Clarifies that a voice or likeness includes a digital replica. Clarifies that false impersonation includes the use of a digital replica with the intent to impersonate another.

Title: Companion Chatbots: Childrens Safety
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Requires an operator of a companion chatbot to do various things with respect to child safety and companion chatbots, including annually performing and documenting a comprehensive risk assessment to identify any child safety risk posed by the design, configuration, and operation of the companion chatbot that assesses, among other things, the likelihood of a covered harm occurring to users.

Title: Pupil Instruction: Preventative Health Instruction
Author: Strickland (R)
Summary: Provides for the Ready to Learn, Ready for Health Act. Requires, when the Health Education Framework for California Public Schools is next revised on or after the specified date, the Instructional Quality Commission to consider including information on evidence based preventative health instruction, including information on nutrition, food literacy, sleep, movement, stress management, and digital balance in an integrated manner that discusses these key health factors and the interrelationship between them.

Title: Digital Dignity Act
Author: Becker (D)
Summary: Enacts the Digital Dignity Act. Provides that subject to specified liability a person who, by distributing content with actual knowledge that the content includes a digital replica, is found guilty of violating a criminal provision for which false impersonation of another is a required element or is found liable in a civil action arising from the use or portrayal through a digital replica.

Title: Advertisement Claims: Health Related Consumer Products
Author: Gonzalez (D)
Topics: Deepfake, Health Use, Notification, Private Sector Use
Summary: Requires, subject to specified exceptions, a person who creates or causes to be created an advertisement that includes the image, audio, or video of a digital replica or synthetic performer depicted as a health care provider that is generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence or other computer technology to promote the sale of a health related consumer product or service to include a clear and conspicuous disclosure that no human health care provider is depicted.

Title: Artificial Intelligence: Transparency and Governance
Author: Cabaldon (D)
Summary: Specifies that, for purposes of the State Public Records Act, the Bagley Keene Open Meeting Act, the Ralph M. Brown Act, the Political Reform Act of 1974, the Administrative Procedure Act, and the California Environmental Quality Act, the terms person, interested person, participant, member of the public, and any other similar terms under each act referring to those who may engage with governmental agencies, do not include artificial intelligence.

Title: Student Personal Information
Author: Addis (D)
Topics: Education Use, Private Sector Use, Provenance
Summary: Applies the provisions of the K-12 Pupil Online Personal Information Protection Act and the Early Learning Personal Information Protection Act to an operator of a website, online service, online application, or mobile application with actual knowledge that the site, service, or application is used for the applicable school purposes and was designed or marketed for those purposes. Enacts the Higher Education Student Information Protection Act. Authorizes a harmed student or pupil to bring a civil action.

Title: Central Valley School Safety Coordination Pilot Program
Author: Hurtado (D)
Summary: Requires the Office of Emergency Services, in consultation with the State Department of Education, to establish the Central Valley School Safety Coordination Pilot Program for the purpose of studying and evaluating improved communication pathways between local educational agencies and regional fusion centers regarding credible safety threats affecting school communities.

Title: Nonconsensual Intimate Image Clearinghouse
Author: Grove (R)
Summary: Requires the Department of Justice to establish the Nonconsensual Intimate Image Clearinghouse to allow individuals who were exploited in the State to submit a request for the removal of nonconsensual intimate images from covered platforms. Requires the department to transmit verified identifiers of images to covered platforms and require those platforms to remove verified matches within 48 hours of receipt and to prevent the images from being uploaded again.

Title: State Agencies: Automated Decision Systems
Author: Cabaldon (D)
Summary: Imposes certain restrictions on the use of an automated decision system by a state agency to confer services, defined as, among other things, the issuance of professional licenses and provision of public benefits.

Title: Crimes: Sexual Exploitation of a Child
Author: Rubio (D)
Summary: Makes a person guilty of a misdemeanor or a felony if the person downloads, streams, or accesses through electronic or digital media material that depicts a person under 18 years of age engaged in an act of sexual conduct, except as specified.

Title: Information Practices Act of 1977
Author: Ward (D)
Summary: Provides that the Information Practices Act of 1977 prescribes a set of requirements, prohibitions, and remedies applicable to agencies with regard to their collection, storage, and disclosure of personal information. Prohibits an agency from using records containing personal information for any purpose or purposes other than the purpose or purposes for which that personal information was collected, except as required or authorized by State law.

Title: Customer Service Chatbots
Author: Zbur (D)
Summary: Prohibits a large private business from representing that a customer service chatbot is a human. Requires the large private business to provide certain disclosures if a reasonable person interacting with the chatbot would be misled to believe they are interacting with a human. Requires a large private business to provide customers with human customer service support and communications within a specified number of minutes of requesting human customer service.

Title: State Bar of California: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Dixon (R)
Summary: Requires the State Bar to disclose, on its internet website, the use of artificial intelligence generated content in developing or administering State Bar examinations. Requires the State Bar to disclose, on the cover page of study materials, the use of artificial intelligence generated content in examination study material it, among other things, publishes or endorses.

Title: Pornographic Internet Websites
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Requires an operator of a pornographic internet website, among other things, to exercise ordinary care and reasonable diligence to ensure that each instance of sexually explicit content displayed on the operator's pornographic internet website does not include a depicted individual. Defines terms, including depicted person, for its purposes.

Title: Health Curriculum Framework: Human Trafficking
Author: Krell (D)
Summary: Requires the Instructional Quality Commission, when the health curriculum framework is next revised on or after January 1, 2027, to consider providing for inclusion in that framework recommendations related to school districts, county offices of education, and charter schools providing annual, developmentally appropriate lessons for each grade served by the local educational agency about how to prevent human trafficking and how to prevent exploitation for labor and services.

Title: Pupil Instruction: Health Framework: Sexual Health
Author: Rodriguez Mi (D)
Summary: Requires the Instructional Quality Commission, during the next revision of the publication �Health Framework for California Public Schools,� to consider including, and recommending for adoption by the State Board of Education, specific content related to sexual health instruction to educate pupils about dating abuse and digital violence.

Title: Workplace Surveillance Tools
Author: Bryan (D)
Topics: Effect on Labor/Employment, Private Sector Use, Responsible Use
Summary: Prohibits an employer from using a workplace surveillance tool on workers for various purposes. Includes preventing compliance with laws or regulations, inferring information about workers engaging in a protected activity, making inferences about an individual's emotional state or based on their gait, or collecting neural data. Prohibits an employer from using facial recognition technology, unless it is used strictly to open a locked device or grant access to locked or secure areas.

Title: Workplace Artificial Intelligence Tools
Author: Schultz (D)
Topics: Effect on Labor/Employment, Private Sector Use, Private Right of Action
Summary: Requires an employer to provide a written notice to a worker that a workplace artificial intelligence tool was used to assist the employer in making employment related decisions or to surveil workers in the workplace. Requires the notice to be given to a worker within a specified time and requires the notice to contain specified information, including the specific employment related decisions likely to be affected by the use of the workplace AI tool. Provides for civil actions for damages.

Title: Reporting Mechanism: Child Sexual Abuse Material
Author: Wicks (D)
Summary: Makes a social media company liable to a depicted individual, as defined, for actual and statutory damages, as provided. Imposes a civil penalty on a noncomplying company to be collected in a civil action by certain public attorneys, including the Attorney General. Establishes the Survivor Support Fund within the state treasury and makes moneys in the fund available, upon appropriation by the Legislature, for grants by the State Victim Compensation Board to community-based organizations.

Title: Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Bonta M (D)
Summary: Requires a health facility, clinic, physician's office, or office or a group practice to ensure that no clinical decision, is based solely on the output of a clinical decision support system, as defined, and that a licensed health care professional exercises independent professional judgment when reviewing and approving a clinical decision that is based on the output of a clinical decision support system.

Title: Companion Chatbots: Crisis Interruption Pauses
Author: Pellerin (D)
Summary: Provides for the Preventing AI User Self Endangerment (PAUSE) Act. Requires an operator of companion chatbots to adopt and make publicly available a policy governing its protocol for identifying and responding to credible crisis expressions and, for each companion chatbot an operator makes available to users in the State, implement a system for monitoring and detecting credible crisis expressions in user conversations with companion chatbots.

Title: Companion Chatbots: Childrens Safety
Author: Wicks (D)
Topics: Health Use, Notification, Private Right of Action
Summary: Relates to artificial intelligence. Requires an operator of a companion chatbot to, on or before specified date to do various things with respect to child safety and companion chatbots, including annually perform and document a comprehensive risk assessment to identify any child safety risk, as defined, posed by the design, configuration, and operation of the companion chatbot that assesses, among other things, the likelihood of a covered harm, as defined, occurring to child users.

Title: Tenancy: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure
Author: Pellerin (D)
Summary: Requires a person who includes a digitally altered image, as defined, in an advertisement or other promotional material for the rental of real property to include a disclosure, as specified.

Title: Worker Data: Prohibitions: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Ward (D)
Topics: Private Sector Use, Private Right of Action
Summary: Prohibits an employer from using a workers personal information to train an artificial intelligence system to replicate, automate, or replace a workers job, and prohibits an employer from selling, disclosing, or otherwise providing access to a workers personal information to a third party for the purpose of training an AI system to replicate, automate, or replace a job. Authorizes a worker who suffered a violation to bring a civil action for damages, injunctive relief, punitive damages, and attorneys fees.

Title: Pupil Instruction: Digital Wellness
Author: Hoover (R)
Summary: Requires the State Department of Education, on or before a specified date, to develop a plan to expand mental health instruction in State public schools. Requires the department, on or before a specified date, to develop a plan to expand digital wellness instruction in the state public schools, as provided.

Title: Elementary and secondary education
Author: Muratsuchi (D)
Summary: Establishes a system of public elementary and secondary education in this state. Requires school districts, county offices of education, and charter schools employ personnel to provide instruction to and services for pupils in kindergarten and grades 1 to 12, inclusive, at school sites throughout the state. Defines, for purposes of the Education Code, both a public school employee and a contractor providing services in a public school to mean a natural person.

Title: Social Media Platforms: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Lowenthal (D)
Summary: Enacts the Digital Choice Act. Requires a social media company or a person that makes an artificial intelligence model available to a third party for use, modification, copying, or combination with other software, defined as a deployer, to allow a consumer to request a copy of the consumer's personal information, contextual data, and social graph and would require the social media company or deployer to respond to that request within five business days.

Title: Postsecondary Education: Sexual Harassment
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Requires, in order to receive State funds for student financial assistance, the governing board of a community college district, the Trustees of the State University, the Regents of the University of California, and the governing boards of independent postsecondary educational institutions to update their sexual harassment policies to include, among other things, a list of organizations to assist students and employees with the removal of digitized sexually explicit material from digital platforms.

Title: Lubricants Waste: Packaging: Producer Responsibility
Author: Rodriguez Mi (D)
Summary: Creates a producer responsibility program for lubricants waste that is not covered by the Oil Recycling Enhancement Act and packaging associated with lubricant products. Requires a producer responsibility organization to provide a convenient collection and management system. Requires the charge be set at an amount that is adequate to cover CalRecycle's and DTSC's actual and reasonable costs of administering and enforcing the program.

Title: Pupil Safety: Nonconsensual Artificial Intimate Images
Author: Lackey (R)
Summary: Requires the State Department of Education to conduct a study on nonconsensual artificial intimate images involving pupils in the specified grades. Requires the study to include, among other things, a summary of the resources for schools regarding nonconsensual artificial intimate images and the effects of nonconsensual artificial intimate images on pupils.

Title: Public Postsecondary Education: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Fong M (D)
Summary: Requires the California Community Colleges and the California State University, and requests the University of California, before providing a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) system to students, faculty, or staff, to as specified, convene a joint working group to present recommendations for procurement standards and training, which the bill would require to be submitted on or before a specified date.

Title: Income Tax: Credits: Commercial Production
Author: Elhawary (D)
Summary: Excludes any commercial that is created entirely by generative artificial intelligence, as specified, or that utilizes generative artificial intelligence, automated technologies, or autonomous vehicles in a manner that replaces or diminishes the job functions customarily performed by a human worker in the production. Requires any bill authorizing a new tax expenditure to contain, among other things, specific goals, purposes, and objectives that the tax expenditure will achieve.

Title: State Agencies or Departments: Public Communications
Status: Pending - Assembly Consent Calendar - Second Legislative Day
Author: Ta (R)
Summary: Provides that existing law requires a State agency or department that utilizes generative artificial intelligence to directly communicate with a person regarding government services and benefits to ensure that those communications include a disclaimer that indicates to the person that the communication was generated by GenAI. Requires that disclaimer when a State agency or department communicates with the public.

Title: Downcoding Medical Claims
Author: Patel (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law sets forth requirements by which a health care service plan or health insurer reimburses a provider for health care services. Requires a determination to downcode a claim, which is the unilateral alteration by a payer of the service or procedure code submitted on a claim resulting in a lower payment, to include a documented review of the clinical information supporting the billed service.

Title: Artificial Intelligence: Education and Workforce
Author: Macedo (R)
Topics: Education Use, Education/Training, Effect on Labor/Employment
Summary: Enacts the Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Development Act to accomplish specified goals, including, among others, empowering and supporting community college instructors in using and deploying artificial intelligence responsibly in administrative and classroom settings, and strengthening the States AI and technology workforce pipeline by upskilling and educating all workers so they can benefit from AI.

Title: Community Colleges: Artificial Intelligence: Pilot
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Topics: Education/Training, Effect on Labor/Employment, Notification, Private Sector Use, Studies
Summary: Relates to the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges. Requires the chancellors office to implement the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program and to select up to a specified number of community college districts to participate in the pilot program. Requires the chancellors office to submit a report to the Legislature evaluating the effectiveness of the pilot program.

Title: Report: Labor Force Impact: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Schiavo (D)
Summary: Establishes the State Artificial Intelligence Worker Impact Data Assessment Project and establishes the State Artificial Intelligence Worker Impact Data Assessment Project Advisory Panel in the Employment Development Department. Requires the EDD, in consultation with the advisory panel, to perform an assessment of data sources and collection methods regarding the use and impact of advanced artificial intelligence systems on the labor force. Requires the advisory panel to submit a report to the Legislature.

Title: Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Ortega (D)
Topics: Health Use, Notification, Private Sector Use
Summary: Requires a health facility, clinic, physician's office, or office of a group practice that uses or deploys a clinical decision support system, as defined, for patient care to provide written notice of required information to any licensed health care professional or other person using a clinical decision support system or viewing outputs from a clinical decision support system.

Title: Crimes: Prostitution
Author: Schultz (D)
Summary: Requires a person who commits prostitution with intent to receive compensation, money, or anything of value from another person to, for a first or second violation of those provisions, be offered a diversion program pursuant to specified provisions.

Title: Small Business Advocate: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Hoover (R)
Summary: Enacts the AI for Main Street Act, which would require the Small Business Advocate to provide assistance to small businesses in evaluating artificial intelligence concerning operations, including by providing information, guidance, and training, developing training materials, and conducting outreach.

Title: State Contracts: Report: Modern Foundation Models
Author: Lee (D)
Summary: Requires the Department of Industrial Relations, in consultation with the Department of Technology, to convene a Foundation Model Labor and Procurement Working Group consisting of 9 members, assess labor practices underlying the development of modern foundation models and associated artificial intelligence systems and develop recommendations regarding whether and how the state should incorporate labor standards into procurement decisions for foundation models and associated artificial intelligence systems.

Title: Public Employees: Notice: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Petrie-Norris (D)
Summary: Relates to the deployment of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools by the State. Requires certain State and local public employers to provide written notice to a recognized employee organization at least a specified number of days before taking an action to develop, purchase, implement, or utilize GenAI to perform a service that is within the scope of work of the job classification represented by the recognized employee organization.

Title: California AI Transparency Act: System Provenance Data
Author: Wicks (D)
Summary: Provides that the State AI Transparency Act requires a large online platform to detect whether any provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards-setting body is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform. Requires a large online platform to detect any system provenance data that is embedded into, attached to, or associated with content.

Title: Classified Workers Rights
Author: Cortese (D)
Summary: Urges President Donald J. Trump and the Congress of the United States to approve federal legislation guaranteeing specified rights to classified workers that would, among other things, empower those workers to work in a stable, safe environment and receive livable and competitive wages.

Title: Employment: Automated Decision Systems
Author: McNerney (D)
Topics: Government Use, Effect on Labor/Employment, Notification
Summary: Requires an employer to provide a written notice that an automated decision system, for the purpose of making employment-related decisions, not including hiring, is in use at the workplace to all workers that will foreseeably be directly affected by the ADS. Requires an employer to notify a job applicant that the employer utilizes an ADS in hiring decisions, if the employer will use the ADS in making decisions for that position. Prohibits an employer from using an ADS that does certain functions.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Technology
Author: Ashby (D)
Topics: Criminal Use, Deepfake, Judicial Use, Private Sector Use
Summary: Defines various terms related to artificial intelligence and digital replication and clarifies that false impersonation includes the use of a digital replica with the intent to impersonate another for purposes of these and other criminal provisions. Requires a specified warning to be hyperlinked on any page or screen where the consumer may input a prompt to the technology and included in the terms and conditions for use of the technology.

Title: February 2025 Bar Exam: Audit
Author: Umberg (D)
Topics: Audit, Judicial Use, Effect on Labor/Employment, Studies
Summary: Relates to the State Bar Act. Requires the State Auditor to conduct an audit of the specified bar exam and to submit the audit as soon as possible to the Board of Trustees of the State Bar, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, and to the Assembly and Senate Committees on Judiciary. Requires the State Bar to provide the California State Auditor with the funding necessary to cover the costs of the audit.

Title: Housing Rental Terms: Algorithmic Devices
Author: Perez S (D)
Summary: Makes it unlawful for any person to sell, license, or provide to a certain number or more persons a rental pricing algorithm with the intent or reasonable expectation that it be used by a specified number or more persons to set rental terms for residential premises. Makes it unlawful for a person to set or adopt rental terms based on the recommendation of a rental pricing algorithm if the person knows or should know that the rental pricing algorithm processes nonpublic competitor data for certain purposes.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Models: Large Developers
Author: Wiener (D)
Topics: Cybersecurity, Government Use, Impact Assessment, Private Sector Use, Studies
Summary: Enacts the Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act. Provides that the TFAIA would exempt from the California Public Records Act a report of a critical safety incident submitted to the Office of Emergency Services, a report of assessments of catastrophic risk from internet use, and a covered employee report made pursuant to the whistleblower protections.

Title: Electrical Corporations: Data Centers: Report
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law authorizes the commission to fix the rates and charges for every public utility and requires that those rates and charges be just and reasonable. Authorizes the Public Utilities Commission to assess the extent to which electrical corporation costs associated with new loads from data centers result in cost shifts to other electrical corporation customers.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Program: Attorney General
Author: McNerney (D)
Summary: Requires the Attorney General to establish and maintain a specified program to build internal expertise in artificial intelligence, including its applications, risks, regulatory implications, and civil rights impacts. Requires, on or before the specified date, and annually thereafter, the Attorney General to submit a public report to the Legislature describing the program, key developments in artificial intelligence law and policy, and recommendations for additional State oversight or safeguards.

Title: Health Care: Legally Protected Health Care Activity
Author: Ward (D)
Summary: Expands the Address Confidentiality Program to a gender-affirming health care provider, employee or volunteer who faces threats of violence or harassment because of affiliation with a gender-affirming health services facility. Prohibits a person, business or association from soliciting, selling or trading on the internet or social media personal information or images of providers, employees, volunteers or patients with certain intent. Prohibits certain reports of testosterone or mifepristone prescriptions.

Title: Public Higher Education: Artificial Intelligence Usage
Status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Higher Education Committee
Author: Niello (R)
Summary: Encourages the President of the University of California, the Chancellor of the California State University, and the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges to create a workgroup of faculty, staff, and administrators to review the use of artificial intelligence in higher education, and create a report and make public the strategies and best practices for artificial intelligence usage agreed upon by the workgroup.

Title: Budget Act of 2025
Status: Pending - Carryover - Senate Budget & Fiscal Review Committee
Author: Gabriel (D)
Summary: Makes appropriations for the support of State government for the specified fiscal year.

Title: Budget Act of 2025
Author: Budget and Fiscal Review Cmt
Summary: Makes appropriations for the support of the government of the State of California and for several public purposes in accordance with the provisions of Section 12 of Article IV of the Constitution of the State of California, relating to the state budget, to take effect immediately, budget bill.

Title: Budget Act of 2025
Author: Budget and Fiscal Review Cmt
Summary: Provides that the Budget Act of 2025 would make appropriations for the support of State government for the specified fiscal year. Amends the Budget Act of 2025 by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.

Title: Budget Act of 2025
Author: Gabriel (D)
Summary: Provides that the Budget Act of 2025 would make appropriations for the support of State government for the specified fiscal year. Amends the Budget Act of 2025 by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes. Provides for the support of, among other things, the Legislative Analyst's Office, the State Court Facilities Construction Fund, the Judicial Branch, local assistance, and the Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development.

Title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, and 2024
Status: Pending - Carryover - Senate Budget & Fiscal Review Committee
Author: Gabriel (D)
Summary: Provides that the Budget Act of 2022, the Budget Act of 2023, and the Budget Act of 2024 made appropriations for the support of State government for the specified fiscal years. Amends those budget acts by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.

Title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, and 2024
Author: Budget and Fiscal Review Cmt
Summary: Provides that the Budget Act of 2022, the Budget Act of 2023, and the Budget Act of 2024 made appropriations for the support of State government for the specified fiscal years. Amends those budget acts by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.

Title: Data Centers: Power Usage Effectiveness: Cost Shifts
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Requires the State Energy Resources Conservation and Development Commission to establish a process for the owner of a data center to submit the power usage effectiveness ratio for the data center to the Energy Commission on a biannual basis. Requires the Energy Commission, as part of the 2027 edition of the Integrated Energy Policy Report, to include an assessment of electrical load trends for data centers.

Title: Workplace Surveillance Tools
Status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee
Author: Smallwood-Cueva (D)
Topics: Effect on Labor/Employment, Private Sector Use
Summary: Requires an employer to annually provide a notice to the Department of Industrial Relations, in the Labor and Workforce Development Agency, of all the workplace surveillance tools the employer is using in the workplace. Requires the notice to include, among other information, the personal information that will be collected from workers and consumers and whether they will have the option of opting out of the collection of personal information.

Title: Community Colleges: Personnel: Qualifications
Author: Cervantes (D)
Summary: Relates to the California Community Colleges. Requires a community college instructor, librarian, counselor, student personnel worker, supervisor, administrator, chief administrative officer, extended opportunity programs and services worker, disabled students programs and services worker, apprenticeship instructor, or supervisor of health to be a person who meets specified minimum qualifications to serve in that position or the alternative qualifications to serve in that position.

Title: Companion Chatbots
Author: Padilla (D)
Topics: Notification, Private Sector Use, Private Right of Action
Summary: Provides that among other things related to making a companion chatbot platform safer for users, if a reasonable person interacting with a companion chatbot would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, require an operator of a companion chatbot platform to issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.

Title: State Bar of California
Author: Umberg (D)
Topics: Education Use, Judicial Use, Effect on Labor/Employment
Summary: Requires the California Lawyers Association or the affiliated 501(c)(3) organization to submit an annual report to the Legislature detailing their use of funds and a statement of compliance with the prohibition on creating, operating, or soliciting members for affinity or royalty programs involving similar products or services.

Title: Fair Online Pricing Act
Author: Wahab (D)
Summary: Provides that the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 grants to a consumer various rights with respect to personal information that is collected by a business. Provides for the Fair Online Pricing Act. Prohibits, subject to specified exceptions, a price offered to a consumer through the consumer's online device from being generated, in whole or in part, based on certain input data, including the presence or absence of any software on the online device.

Title: School Libraries: Model Library Standards
Author: Patel (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law requires the State Board of Education to adopt standards, rules, and regulations for school library services. Requires the Superintendent of Public Instruction to consider recommending revisions to the standards for school library services to the State Board. Requires the Superintendent to convene a group of experts to assist the Superintendent in developing revisions. Requires the Superintendent, in consultation with the Instructional Quality Commission, to hold public hearings.

Title: California Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
Status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Third Reading File
Author: Hurtado (D)
Summary: Enacts the California Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025. Prohibits person from distributing or making recommendations based on the use of a pricing algorithm to a specified number or more competitors if the person knows or should know that the pricing algorithm processes competitor data. Establishes an affirmative defense to liability under this prohibition for a person who demonstrates by a preponderance of evidence that they exercised reasonable due diligence.

Title: Artificial Intelligence: Defenses
Author: Krell (D)
Summary: Prohibits a defendant who developed, modified, or used artificial intelligence from asserting a defense that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff.

Title: Cartwright Act: Violations
Author: Aguiar-Curry (D)
Summary: Makes it unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce. Makes it unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of the state.

Title: Data Brokers: Data Collection and Deletion
Author: Becker (D)
Summary: Requires a data broker to provide additional information to the agency, including whether the data broker collects consumers' names, dates of birth, zip Codes, email addresses, phone numbers, login or account information, various government identification numbers, mobile advertising, connected television, or vehicle identification numbers, citizenship data, union membership status, sexual orientation status, gender identity and gender expression data, and biometric data.

Title: Employment: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Smallwood-Cueva (D)
Topics: Government Use, Effect on Labor/Employment, Studies
Summary: Requires the Department of General Services to contract with the University of California, Los Angeles Labor Center to conduct a study evaluating the impact of artificial intelligence on worker well being, job quality, job types, different populations, and State revenues. Requires the department, on or before the specified date, to submit a report of the findings of the study to the Legislature. Repeals these provisions upon submission of that report.

Title: Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act: Prohibition
Author: Wahab (D)
Summary: Provides for the Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act. Prohibits a person from selling, licensing, providing, or price-setting algorithm with the intent or reasonable expectation that it be used by a specified number or more competitors in the same market if the person knows or should know that the algorithm processes nonpublic data to set either a price or supply level of a good or service or a rent or occupancy level of rental property. Provides a user of such algorithm an affirmative defense.

Title: Pornographic Internet Websites: Consent
Author: Dixon (R)
Summary: Requires a person who operates a website to exercise ordinary care and reasonable diligence to ensure that any sexually explicit content uploaded to the operator's pornographic internet website does not include a depicted individual. Requires an operator of a pornographic website to verify a user's email address before permitting the user to upload sexually explicit content to the operator's website. Authorizes a depicted individual and a public prosecutor to bring a civil action to enforce such provisions.

Title: Bots: Disclosure
Author: Wilson (D)
Summary: Requires a person who uses a bot to autonomously communicate with another to ensure that the bot discloses to any person with whom the bot communicates when the bot first communicates with the person that the bot is a bot and not a human being. Authorizes the Attorney General, a district attorney, a county counsel, a city attorney, or a city prosecutor to bring a civil action to punish noncompliance.

Title: Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Relates to copyrighted materials. Requires a developer of a generative artificial intelligence model to document any covered materials that the developer knows were used by the developer to train the model. Requires the developer to make available a mechanism on the developer's website allowing a rights owner to submit a request for information. Authorizes a rights owner who complies with specified requirements for submitting a request that is not provided with information to bring a civil action.

Title: Automated Decision Systems
Status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee
Author: Padilla (D)
Topics: Government Use, Impact Assessment, Private Sector Use
Summary: Requires a developer or a deployer of a high-risk automated decision system to perform an impact assessment before making it publicly available or deploying it. Authorizes the Attorney General or the Civil Rights Department to allow a developer or deployer to cure certain violations. Prohibits an agency from awarding a contract for a high-risk automated decision system unless the person to whom the contract is awarded has certified that the system does not violate, among other civil rights laws, this bill.

Title: State Government: Efficiency of Public Sector
Author: Cabaldon (D)
Summary: States the intent of the Legislature to enact legislation that would lessen the time, effort, money, and programmatic expertise of local public sector workers in compliance with state reporting and permit processing, as specified.

Title: High-risk Artificial Intelligence Systems
Author: Becker (D)
Summary: Imposes a duty on a covered deployer, defined as a business that deploys a high-risk artificial intelligence system that processes personal information, to protect personal information held by the covered deployer, subject to certain requirements.

Title: Health Care Professions: Deceptive Terms or Letters
Author: Bonta M (D)
Summary: Prohibits the use by artificial intelligence or generative artificial intelligence technology of certain terms, letters, or phrases that indicate or imply that the advice, care, reports, or assessments being provided through AI or GenAI is being provided by a natural person with the appropriated health care license or certificate. Makes a violation of these provisions subject to the jurisdiction of the appropriate health care profession board.

Title: Elections: Deceptive Media In Advertisements
Author: Pellerin (D)
Summary: Sets forth additional requirements relating to the color and font size of the disclosure's text. Exempts an election communication from the prohibition if the content includes a disclosure stating that the communication has been generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence. Exempts an advertisement or other election communication from these prohibitions if a reasonable person would understand that the content was satire or parody.

Title: Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Weber (D)
Summary: Specifies that the Department of Public Health is not required to independently inspect, test, or evaluate the functionality of an artificial intelligence system. Requires, beginning January 1, 2027, developers to provide a report identifying compliance efforts with the specified provisions to the department before making an artificial intelligence system commercially or publicly available to a deployer.

Title: Health Care Coverage: Prior Authorization
Author: Harabedian (D)
Summary: Provides for the Medi-Cal program, administered by the State Department of Health Care Services and under which qualified low-income individuals receive health care services, including pursuant to contracts with various types of managed care plans. Authorizes a health care service plan, including a Medi-Cal managed care plan, or disability insurer to use utilization review, under which a licensed physician or a licensed health care professional who is competent to evaluate specific clinical issues.

Title: Law Enforcement Agencies: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Arreguin (D)
Summary: Requires each law enforcement agency to maintain a policy to require an official report prepared by a law enforcement officer or any member of a law enforcement agency that is generated using artificial intelligence either fully or partially to include specified information, including a disclosure statement and the signature of the law enforcement officer or member of a law enforcement agency who prepared the official report. Requires an agency utilizing artificial intelligence to generate a first draft.

Title: Reproductive Health Emergency Preparedness Program
Author: Krell (D)
Summary: Establishes the Reproductive Health Emergency Preparedness Program for the purpose of expanding and improving access to reproductive and sexual health care in emergency departments across the State. Requires the Department of Health Care Access and Information to award the grants and administer the RHEPP. Requires the department to establish minimum standards, funding schedules, and procedures for awarding grants. Limits the permissible uses of grant funds.

Title: Food Delivery Platforms: Customer Service
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Requires a food delivery platform to provide a full refund to the customer if an order is not delivered or the wrong order is delivered, unless the food delivery platform determines that the customer was responsible for the nondelivery or finds evidence indicating the refund request may be fraudulent. Requires the food delivery platform to refund the amount of the original paid gratuity to the customer but to not take or deduct the original gratuity amount from the delivery driver.

Title: Mental Health and Artificial Intelligence
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Requires the Secretary of Government Operations to appoint a mental health and artificial intelligence working group that would evaluate certain issues to determine the role of artificial intelligence in mental health settings. Requires the working group to take input from various stakeholder groups, including health organizations and academic institutions, and conduct at least a specified number of public meetings.

Title: Deepfake Pornography
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law grants to a depicted individual a cause of action against a person who creates and intentionally discloses sexually explicit material. Grants to a depicted individual a cause of action against a person who knows, or reasonably should know, that the depicted individual was a minor when the digitized sexually explicit material was created. Grants a cause of action to that depicted individual against a person who knowingly facilitates or recklessly aids or abets prohibited conduct.

Title: California Education and Workforce Development
Author: Padilla (D)
Summary: Relates to the State Career Technical Education Incentive Grant Program. Requires successful applicants to demonstrate a holistic approach to providing career technical education and career pathways. Requires the department to consult with the California Education Interagency Council instead of the chancellor for those purposes.

Title: Health Care Coverage Reporting
Author: Ortega (D)
Summary: Requires a health care service plan or health insurer that imposes prior authorization to report specified prior authorization data from the previous calendar year on its internet website on or before February 1, 2026, for health care service plans, on or before February 1, 2028, for health insurers, and annually on or before February 1 thereafter. Requires a health care service plan or health insurer to annually report specified claims and prior authorization data to the relevant department.

Title: Privacy: Use of a Person's Name
Author: Cortese (D)
Summary: Provides that a party seeking relief may also seek an injunction or temporary restraining order according to specified procedures. Requires the respondent to comply with the order within 2 business days from the day the order is served, unless otherwise required by the order, if the court grants the applicant a temporary restraining order without notice to the opposing party that requires the respondent to remove, recall, or otherwise cease the publication.

Title: Real Estate: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure
Author: Pellerin (D)
Topics: Deepfake, Housing, Notification, Private Sector Use, Provenance
Summary: Requires a real estate broker or salesperson, or person acting on their behalf, who includes a digitally altered image in an advertisement or other promotional material for the sale of real property to include a specified disclosure. Requires, if the advertisement or promotional material is posted on an internet website, the same image without digital alteration to be included.

Title: Personal Rights: Liability: Social Media Platforms
Author: Stern (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law prohibits a person from using violence or intimidation to interfere with another person's enjoyment of certain rights or because of certain attributes of that person. Makes a social media platform that violates the provisions of law relating to personal rights through its algorithms that relay content to users or aids, abets, acts in concert, or conspires in violation of those laws, liable for specified civil penalties. Provides that such provisions are severable.

Title: Multistakeholder Regulatory Organizations
Author: McNerney (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law requires the Department of Technology to conduct a comprehensive inventory of all high risk automated decision systems that have been proposed for use, development or procurement by, or are being used, developed, or procured by, a State agency. Establishes a process by which the Attorney General designates a private entity as a multistakeholder regulatory organization. Authorizes the Attorney General to establish a fee structure for charging fees to applicants and designated MROs.

Title: Critical Infrastructure: Automated Decision Systems
Author: McNerney (D)
Summary: Provides that existing law requires the Technology Recovery Plan element of the State Administrative Manual to ensure the inclusion of cybersecurity strategy incident response standards. Requires an operator responsible for operating, managing, overseeing, or controlling access to critical infrastructure, that deploys a covered artificial intelligence (AI) system to establish a human oversight mechanism that ensures a human monitors the system's operations in real time.

Title: California AI Transparency Act
Author: Wicks (D)
Summary: Requires a large online platform to, among other things, related to the provenance of content on the platform, detect whether any provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards-setting body is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform. Prohibits, beginning on specified date, a GenAI system hosting platform from knowingly making available a GenAI system that does not place disclosure.

Title: Public Safety Omnibus
Author: Public Safety Cmt
Summary: Renames the Prison Industry Authority as the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Authority, would rename the Prison Industry Board as the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Board, would rename the Prison Industries Revolving Fund as the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Revolving Fund, and would require that any reference to the Prison Industry Authority be deemed a reference to the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Authority.

Title: Pupil Instruction: High Schools: Computer Science
Author: Berman (D)
Summary: Establishes the California Computer Science Demonstration Grant Program for specified purposes, including increasing the number of public high schools offering a computer science course to increase pupil access to computer science education and increasing the computer science course access of pupils eligible for free or reduced-priced meals and pupils that are underrepresented in the field of computer science.

Title: California Cybersecurity Integration Center: AI
Author: Irwin (D)
Summary: Requires the State Cybersecurity Integration Center to develop, in consultation with the Office of Information Security and the Government Operations Agency, a State AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook to facilitate information sharing across the cyber and artificial intelligence communities and to strengthen collective cyber defenses against emerging threats. Requires the center to review federal requirements, standards, and industry best practices, and to use those resources to inform the playbook.

Title: Automated Decision Systems
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Topics: Audit, Education/Training, Health Use, Housing, Impact Assessment, Effect on Labor/Employment, Notification, Private Sector Use, Responsible Use
Summary: Requires a deployer of a covered automated decision system to take certain actions, including conduct impact assessments of the covered ADS and provide deployers to whom the developer transfers the covered ADS with certain information, including a high-level summary of the results of those impact assessments.

Title: Dept. of Fish and Wildlife: San Gabriel Valley
Author: Harabedian (D)
Summary: Establishes the San Gabriel Valley Bear Management and Community Safety Act, which would require, on or before January 1, 2027, the Department of Fish and Wildlife to develop a regional plan specific to the cities located within the San Gabriel Valley in the County of Los Angeles to address issues relating to bears in the community. Requires the plan to include various components, including, among other things, an overview of the behaviors of the bears in the San Gabriel Mountains.

Title: Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Provides for the Leading Ethical AI Development for Kids Act. Prohibits a person, partnership, corporation, business entity, or state or local government agency that makes a companion chatbot available to users from making a companion chatbot available to a child unless the companion chatbot is not foreseeably capable of doing certain things that could harm a child, including encouraging the child to engage in self-harm, suicidal ideation, violence, consumption of drugs or alcohol, or disordered eating.

Title: Reporting Mechanism: Child Sexual Abuse Material
Author: Krell (D)
Topics: Child Pornography, Deepfake, Private Sector Use
Summary: Provides that existing law requires a social media platform to take certain actions with respect to child sexual abuse material on the social media platform, including by requiring the platform to provide a means for a user who is a State resident to report material. Requires a social media company to ensure review by a natural person if there is not an established or known hash match to child sexual abuse material with respect to the reported material and the reported material is not otherwise blocked.

Title: Student Personal Information
Status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee
Author: Addis (D)
Summary: Applies the provisions of the K-12 Pupil Online Personal Information Protection Act and the Early Learning Personal Information Protection Act to an operator of a website, online service, online application, or mobile application with actual knowledge that the site, service, or application is used for the applicable school purposes and was designed or marketed for those purposes. Enacts the Higher Education Student Information Protection Act. Authorizes a harmed student or pupil to bring a civil action.

Title: Maintenance of the Codes
Author: Dixon (R)
Topics: Cybersecurity, Education Use, Education/Training, Private Sector Use, Provenance
Summary: Makes nonsubstantive changes in various provisions of the law to effectuate the recommendations made by the Legislative Counsel to the Legislature.

Title: Language Access
Author: Nguyen (D)
Summary: Relates to the Dymally-Alatorre Bilingual Services Act. Revises the definition of substantial number of non-English-speaking people to include the higher of either the people served by or eligible to be served by a State agency. Requires the State Health and Human Services Agency to designate a Language Access Director to ensure individuals with limited English proficiency and individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing have meaningful access to government programs and services.

Title: Workplace Surveillance
Author: Elhawary (D)
Topics: Effect on Labor/Employment, Private Sector Use
Summary: Limits the use of workplace surveillance tools by employers, including by prohibiting an employer from monitoring or surveilling workers in employee-only, employer-designated areas. Provides workers with the right to leave behind workplace surveillance tools that are on their person or in their possession during off-duty hours. Prohibits a worker from removing or physically tampering with any component of a workplace surveillance tool that is part of or embedded in employer equipment or vehicles.

Title: Information Practices Act of 1977
Author: Ward (D)
Summary: Provides that the Information Practices Act of 1977 prescribes a set of requirements, prohibitions, and remedies applicable to agencies with regard to their collection, storage, and disclosure of personal information. Prohibits an agency from using records containing personal information for any purpose or purposes other than the purpose or purposes for which that personal information was collected, except as required or authorized by State law.

Title: Artificial Intelligence: Auditors: Enrollment
Author: Bauer-Kahan (D)
Summary: Requires the Government Operations Agency to establish a mechanism on the agency's website allowing artificial intelligence auditors to enroll with the agency and allowing natural persons to report misconduct by an enrolled AI auditor. Requires the agency to publish information provided by an enrolled AI auditor on the agency's website, retain specified reports, and share reports submitted by persons reporting misconduct with other State agencies. Requires an AI auditor to enroll with the agency.

Title: Large Load Data Centers
Author: Kipp (D)
Summary: Concerns measure to ensure accountability for large load data centers.

Title: Data Center and Utility Modernization
Author: Valdez A (D)
Summary: Concerns facilitation of data center development while supporting utility resources, creates the State data center workforce, clean energy, grid modernization, and consumer and environmental protection act.

Title: Regulate Earned Wage Access Services
Author: Camacho (D)
Summary: Concerns the regulation of earned wage access services.

Title: Prohibit Use of Personally Identifying Feature
Status: Pending - House State, Civic, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee
Author: Bottoms (R)
Summary: Concerns prohibiting the use of another individual's personally identifying feature without permission.

Title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Health Care
Author: Joseph (D)
Summary: Requires entities that use an artificial intelligence system or algorithm for utilization review to ensure that the system complies with certain requirements, relates to the unauthorized practice of psychotherapy, requires disclosure of a clients right to consent to a disclosure of confidential communications, prohibits a health insurance carrier and a payer of services under the Medical Assistance Act and the Childrens Basic Health Plan Act from paying for psychotherapy services conducted by an AI system.

Title: Psychotherapy Artificial Intelligence Restrictions
Author: Rydin (D)
Summary: Prohibits psychologists, professional counselors, social workers, clinical social workers, marriage and family therapists, addiction counselors, unlicensed psychotherapists and other individuals lawfully permitted to provide psychotherapy services in the State from using an artificial intelligence system to directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication, generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review by regulated professionals, or to detect mental states.

Title: Unfair or Deceptive Trade Practices
Author: Bacon (D)
Summary: Prohibits discrimination against a consumer or worker through the use of automated decision systems used to engage in individualized price setting based on surveillance data regarding a consumer, prohibits individualized wage setting based on such data regarding a worker, specifies activities that are not prohibited as individualized price or wage setting based on surveillance data regarding a consumer or worker, provides that the Attorney General or a district attorney may bring certain civil actions.

Title: Conversational Artificial Intelligence Service Operator
Author: Camacho (D)
Topics: Health Use, Notification, Private Sector Use
Summary: Concerns requirements for an operator of a conversational artificial intelligence service, defines a conversational artificial intelligence service as an artificial intelligence system that is accessible to the general public and that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through textual, visual, or aural communications.

Title: Increase Transparency for Algorithmic Systems
Author: Rodriguez (D)
Topics: Health Use, Housing, Notification, Private Sector Use, Responsible Use
Summary: Concerns measures effective no later than June 30, 2026, to increase transparency for algorithmic systems.

Title: Tech Neutral Anti Discrimination Clarification Act
Author: Baisley (R)
Topics: Education Use, Housing, Effect on Labor/Employment, Responsible Use
Summary: Concerns clarifying anti-discrimination protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.

Title: Detection Components for Wildfire Mitigation
Author: Daugherty (D)
Summary: Requires the division of fire prevention and control in the Department of Public Safety to establish public-private agreements with one or more private partners, by which agreements the state may allocate responsibility or risk to one or more private partners to develop and operate wildfire detection components.

Title: Applying Artificial Intelligence to Fight Wildfire
Author: Baisley (R)
Summary: Concerns the application of artificial intelligence, predicts, prevents, or assists in fighting wildfires, makes an appropriation.

Title: Protections for Users of Social Media
Author: Frizell (R)
Summary: Concerns protections for users of social media, and, in connection therewith, establishing certain requirements for social media companies, provides that general assembly finds that self-regulation by social media companies has not worked, and it is time for the State to step in and put common-sense laws in place to protect its youth, directs social media companies to provide annual data about minors' use of social media platforms, including metrics concerning criminal activity.

Title: Extend Prohibition on School Facial Recognition
Author: Daugherty (D)
Summary: Concerns the limited use of facial recognition services by schools, provides that for a product, device, or software application that allows for analysis of facial features for educational purposes in conjunction with curricula, allows for the analysis of facial features to identify a person who has made a significant threat against a school or the occupants of a school, or to identify a missing student.

Title: Electronic Discovery in Criminal Cases Task Force
Author: Bridges (D)
Summary: Relates to the creation of the Electronic Discovery in Criminal Cases Task Force, provides that the task force consists of a specified number of task force members, provides that the purpose of the task force is to study the costs and management of electronic discovery in criminal cases.

Title: Data Center Development and Grid Modernization Act
Author: Hinrichsen (D)
Summary: Concerns benefits to facilitate data center development while supporting electric grid infrastructure, creates the State data center development and grid modernization act.

Title: Intimate Digital Depictions Criminal Civil Actions
Author: Rodriguez (D)
Topics: Child Pornography, Criminal Use, Deepfake, Notification, Private Right of Action
Summary: Concerns preventing certain disclosures of intimate depictions, creates a cause of action for nonconsensual disclosure of an intimate digital depiction and adding and amending related provisions in criminal law.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protections
Author: Rodriguez (D)
Topics: Government Use, Impact Assessment, Effect on Labor/Employment, Private Sector Use, Responsible Use
Summary: Concerns consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.

Title: Pricing Coordination Between Landlords
Author: Woodrow (D)
Summary: Prohibits a landlord from subscribing to, contracting with, or exchanging any form of consideration in return for the services of a coordinator, prohibits a coordinator from facilitating an agreement among landlords that restricts competition, prohibits two or more landlords from engaging in consciously parallel pricing coordination, provides that a violation is punishable in accordance with the State Antitrust Act of 2023, requires the Division of Housing to develop a public education program.

Title: Consumer Protections and Artificial Intelligence System
Author: Lindstedt (D)
Topics: Education Use, Government Use, Notification, Private Sector Use
Summary: Concerns implementing consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Systems
Author: Weinberg (R)
Topics: Effect on Labor/Employment, Private Sector Use
Summary: Concerns artificial intelligence systems.

Title: Statewide Government Language Access Assessment
Author: Velasco (D)
Summary: Requires the Department of Personnel, in collaboration with the Office of New Americans, to conduct or contract to conduct a statewide language access assessment, specifies what the assessment must identify, including the needs of principal departments to meet the language access standards, provides that the department may enter into an agreement with a third party entity to conduct all or part of the assessment, appropriates funds to the department for use by the State Equity Office.

Title: Public Safety Protections Artificial Intelligence
Author: Rutinel (D)
Topics: Effect on Labor/Employment, Notification, Private Sector Use, Private Right of Action
Summary: Concerns public safety protection from the risks of artificial intelligence systems.

Title: Prohibits Intimate Personal Data Automated Analysis
Author: Mabrey (D)
Topics: Criminal Use, Private Sector Use, Responsible Use
Summary: Concerns limiting the use of automated analysis of intimate personal data to make inferences that impact a person's financial position.

Title: Social Media Tools for Minor Users Parents
Author: Caldwell (R)
Summary: Concerns tools to protect minor users of social media.

Title: Consumer Privacy
Author: Looney (D)
Summary: Concerns consumer privacy and protection, requires the controller to perform its responsibility to respond to a consumer's rights when the controller processes that consumer's personal data by automated means, applies when such data is used for profiling to make a solely automated decision that results in either providing or denying an employment opportunity, prohibits controller to sell, share or transfer, or allow any other person to access, precise geolocation data.

Title: Online Safety
Author: Looney (D)
Topics: Health Use, Notification, Private Sector Use
Summary: Concerns online safety, establishes various requirements concerning artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence systems, artificial intelligence technologies, artificial intelligence companions and automated employment-related decision processes and an Artificial Intelligence Policy Office to be overseen by an Artificial Intelligence Policy Director, requires subscription-based artificial intelligence providers to make consumer disclosure.

Title: Artificial Intelligence
Author: Office of the Governor
Topics: Government Use, Notification, Private Sector Use
Summary: Addresses innovations in and the responsible use of artificial intelligence.

Title: Definition of Child Sexual Abuse Material
Author: Joint Judiciary
Summary: Concerns the definition of child sexual abuse material, expands the definition of child sexual abuse material, provides for the definition of a visual depiction of a subject when described as indistinguishable, excludes the definition to a visual depiction that is a drawing, cartoon, sculpture or painting of a person under sixteen years of age.

Title: Disclosure of the Residential Address of Public School
Author: Government Oversight Committee
Summary: Prohibits the disclosure of the residential address of public school employees under the freedom of information act, establishes a task force concerning mass requests under the act.

Title: Health Coverage
Author: Joint Insurance and Real Estate
Summary: Requires health carriers and preferred provider networks that contract with providers to pay equal reimbursement rates for certain outpatient services to all providers in a geographic area, clarifies that health carriers and health plan administrators may use certain utilization management tools, relates to anti steering clauses, prohibits insurers from requiring step therapy for prescription drugs used to treat all forms of cancer and certain diseases, relates to algorithmic or automatic claim downcoding.

Title: Department of Economic and Community Development
Author: Joint Commerce
